root_cause: audit.ts carried a self-documented FORWARD-OBLIGATION comment since T-0138 (export)/T-0500 (the real journal): 'no PDP gate in dev slice... all three routes must be closed together.' Investigation for this task found the three routes were NOT uniformly gated: GET /api/audit already had a real owner-only authz check (loadAdminContext + holdsAuditRead, added by T-0500's review) but it lived inside handleGetAuditLog, a module-scope helper defined BEFORE registerAuditRoutes' first .register( call -- invisible to ci/checks/actor-active-route-coverage.sh's block-scoped text scan (the SAME limitation class ADR-T0726 §2.4 documents for notification-prefs.ts/solution-publish.ts), which is why it still showed as a live finding. GET /api/audit/export only verified an x-dev-user header was PRESENT (any tenant member in dev mode, or any authenticated caller in keycloak mode) -- never WHO. GET /api/audit/:instanceId had NO gate whatsoever: withAuth's dev-mode branch is a documented no-op (src/http/auth.ts:402-406, 'dev pass-through... no token required'), and this route performed no additional check of its own -- a completely unauthenticated request in dev mode received the full demo instance trace.
resolver_reused: loadAdminContext (src/db/org.ts) -- one of the 7 registered AUTHORITY_RESOLVERS in ci/checks/actor-authority-deactivation-gate.sh (T-0658/T-0662), already carrying the ACTOR_ACTIVE_SQL (`deactivated_at IS NULL`) predicate, already used by GET /api/audit itself since T-0500. No second authority path was introduced: the fix reuses the EXACT SAME loadAdminContext call + holdsAuditRead(admin) === admin.isGenesisOwner boolean the pre-existing gate used, now via one shared function (requireAuditRead) called by all three routes.
who_may_read_audit: genesis-owner ONLY -- the SAME policy T-0500's review already established for GET /api/audit ('a mgmt_object:* grant covers a SINGLE object type [department/position/employee] and MUST NOT open the entire journal', per the file's own in-code comment). Investigated whether a narrower or broader policy made sense for /export and /:instanceId specifically (they serve DEMO/fixture data, not the real audit_event table) -- concluded the file's OWN FORWARD-OBLIGATION comment explicitly groups all three under one policy ('all three routes must be closed together'), and there is no product signal anywhere (grep across web/src for any non-owner audit-reading UI surface came up empty -- the only export caller, shell.jsx's downloadAuditLog, has no owner-only frontend gate either, meaning the backend fix is the FIRST enforcement point) to justify diverging the two demo routes from the real journal's policy. Reusing the identical policy for all three is the more defensible, lower-surface-area choice.
denial_policy: 403 ADMIN_GATE_REJECTED for an authenticated-but-unauthorized caller (not honest-404) on all three routes -- direct precedent: GET /api/audit itself (T-0500) already established 403/401 as this poverhnost's own authz shape (distinct from T-0721's /api/processes/:id, which deliberately chose 404 to hide record EXISTENCE). The existence of a tenant's audit log is not a secret the way a specific record row is, so there is no additional guarantee 404 would buy here, and diverging from the already-established sibling-route precedent inside the SAME file/SAME gate would be pure inconsistency. 401 UNAUTHENTICATED fires earlier (extractActor) for a caller with no resolvable identity at all. 503 AUDIT_UNAVAILABLE fires first of all when no DB pool is wired (memory mode) -- the gate itself needs a DB read to resolve admin context, so it cannot fail open; this mirrors GET /api/audit's own pre-existing 503-without-a-store behavior, now extended to all three routes since the gate (not just the data) now needs a DB.

friction_events: T-0737/docs/tasks/T-0726.adr.md's own §5.2 finding text (and the parent task prompt quoting it) describes GET /api/audit as un-gated ('весь аудит-журнал тенанта... читается любым членом'), but reading src/http/audit.ts showed it already had a real owner-only gate since T-0500 -- the coverage-gate finding was a FALSE NEGATIVE (module-scope-helper blind spot, ADR-T0726 §2.4 point 1), not an actual open hole.
